reuse.why: The change reuses the existing recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, although schedule construction and adjusted-date enumeration remain assembled separately by consumers.

duplication.why: The new range handler repeats the existing upcoming-dates handler's schedule construction and occurrence-to-adjusted-day pipeline.

placement.why: Recurrence policies remain in shared/schedules.ts, configuration lives in the existing model, and the new endpoint resides in the schedules server module.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the four requested scheduling changes, their consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared helpers provide useful reuse, but separate recurrence assembly and calendar-dependent holiday expansion with an arbitrary fifty-year horizon make the design harder to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers continue to use recurConfigToRSchedule and the existing weekend adjustment helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated construction and date-adjustment pipeline is direct repetition rather than duplication concealed through restructuring.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts adds a holidays parameter to applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; adds daily weekend filtering, a weekend-only interval exception, and yearly holiday expansion; no changed consumer bypasses the shared helpers.
